newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail firm tries to prevent strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail firm tries to prevent strike.

text.p: State-owned Croatian Railways (HZ) management said on Thursday it had met representatives of workers in an attempt to defuse tensions and prevent a strike.
"The management believes that the strike would have a negative effect on the resolution of HZ's status," it said in a statement released through the national news agency Hina.
The two sides set up a joint committee to rule in a dispute about the loss-making company's restructuring plans, that are soon coming up for debate by Croatia's parliament.
But it was not clear whether the railmen's union revoked a call for a general strike on November 28 over their poor status after the government announced a cut in next year's subsidy.

In its 1997 budget draft it proposed to slash help to HZ to under one billion kuna. That effectively ruled out any possibility of an additional pay rise, aside an increase of a few percent due to an income tax cut from next January.
